subject.title: fix(gmail): stop watcher when OAuth renewal is invalid

question: Should terminal Gog OAuth renewal errors intentionally stop both gateway-managed and foreground Gmail watcher processes, rather than leaving the listener running in a degraded state?
rationale: Both outcomes can make stale coverage visible, but terminating an existing process changes operator-visible lifecycle behavior and requires confirmation that this fail-closed boundary is the supported product behavior.

options.title: Stop on verified terminal OAuth errors
options.body: Accept the shared stop behavior after live proof confirms exact invalid-grant handling and preservation of transient retries.

options.title: Keep a degraded listener state
options.body: Retain the process but expose explicit unhealthy status and bounded renewal behavior if process continuity is the preferred compatibility contract.

recommendation.title: Stop on verified terminal OAuth errors
recommendation.body: Accept the shared stop behavior after live proof confirms exact invalid-grant handling and preservation of transient retries.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice governs gateway lifecycle and compatibility behavior across both public Gmail watcher entry points.
